column1: # Deliberate exceptions to Swift <-> Kotlin `pickLanguage` literal parity (#1295).
# The invariant: the shipped Swift engine and the ADR-023 `commonMain` Kotlin
# port render the same model-facing prompt text, so a behaviour comparison
# between them measures the engines and not two different prompts. Enforcement is
# scripts/check-prompt-literal-parity.py (pre-commit sub-gate + the CI
# "Shell gate tests" job). This file is the escape hatch, and every row is a
# claim that a divergence is intended.
# Format: <side>\t<stem>\t<digest>\t<excerpt>\t<reason>   ('#' lines and blanks skipped)
#   side     swift-only | kotlin-only | unported
#            swift-only / kotlin-only  — this (ja, en) pair exists on one side only.
#            unported                  — the whole Swift file has no Kotlin
#                                        counterpart yet; digest/excerpt are `-`.
#   stem     the Swift basename with any `+Extension` suffix stripped, i.e. the
#            name the two sides are paired by (`PromptBuilder+PrivateSections.swift`
#            and `PromptBuilder.kt` both reduce to `PromptBuilder`).
#   digest   sha256(ja \0 en)[:12] of the NORMALIZED pair. Keyed on both halves on
#            purpose: editing either one invalidates the row, so a reworded
#            deferral gets re-approved instead of coasting. A literal is not
#            usable as a key — a `"""` block carries real newlines and tabs.
#            **`unported` rows carry no digest and so are NOT pinned**: such a row
#            exempts every literal in that file, including ones added after it was
#            approved. It expires only when the Kotlin counterpart appears (which
#            the checker reports as stale). Keep them scarce.
#   excerpt  a readable, escaped prefix of the ja literal. Cosmetic; the digest is
#            what matches. `<>` marks an erased interpolation.
#   reason   why the divergence is intended. Required; a blank fails the gate.
# The checker prints the exact row to paste when it finds a divergence, and it
# fails on a row that no longer matches anything — a healed divergence must drop
# its row rather than linger as a standing exemption.
